history: Brannock was settled by miners who came for Cinder and stayed because the ore never ran out. The first crews lived in the hulls of the ships that brought them. When the hulls wore out, the crews bolted them to rock and called the result a habitat. Most of the hab rings in the system are still those first hulls, patched so often that nobody can say what is original.

The rest followed the ore. Tugs hauled it out to Tallow, a grey moon of the gas giant Vast, and a refinery grew there. A yard went up in the girders of Kettle to turn the metal into ships. Halde, with its cold coast and its clouds, became the place where people raised children and spent their wages. It was the only world in the system where a person could walk outside without a suit or a sunscreen.

The Ironhulls keep Brannock as a working system and have never made it much more. The Federation's navy passes through and takes its cut in inspections. Blackhulls drink in the docks and are not asked about their cargo. Prism's agents come for contracts and leave without friends. Nobody here calls this a golden age, but the lifts still run.
culture: People in Brannock measure each other by what they can fix. A good welder gets a drink bought for her, and a clean-handed visitor gets a look. They speak shortly, swear mildly, and tease newcomers with the old names, rusters and rockheads, until the newcomer answers in kind. Then the teasing stops. Outsiders are tolerated if they pay, and trusted if they turn up with the right part at the right time. Nothing is thrown away. A broken thing is a future patch, and a dead ship is a shopping list.

artBible.lighting: Low orange starlight from a dim sun, and sodium lamps that turn every shadow brown. Welding arcs flash blue-white in the gloom. Refinery flares throw moving orange light across grey surfaces.
artBible.architecture: Modular boxes and drums welded to girders or bolted to bare rock. Hab rings are clamped onto cliffs and asteroids. Walkways are added wherever someone needed one, and ladders and cable runs cross every wall.
artBible.materials: Rust-streaked plate, weld seams left visible, riveted patches in mismatched greys and browns. Cable, chain, scored steel, stained concrete, and cracked sealant gone yellow.
artBible.mood: Tired, practical, and warm at the edges. It is a place where hard work is done and nobody is impressed by it.
artBible.design: Ironhull design is welded, modular, rusted and patched. Every structure has been repaired many times, and the repairs are never hidden. Sodium-lamp orange marks everything that is lit, and hab rings are bolted straight onto rock.

description: Cinder Deep is a mine and nothing else. The planet sits too close to its star, so the day side cooks, and the crews live and work on the night side. The shafts follow the ore into the rock, and the tunnels bend with the seams. They were never drawn up, only dug. The hab modules sit in the tunnel mouths like barnacles, their plating scorched at one end and frosted at the other.

The ore goes up the lift to waiting tugs, and the tugs bring back what the crews cannot make. Food, water and spare parts come down, and so do consumer goods and medicine. Anyone who arrives with a hold full of those is welcome. Anyone who wants ore will find it cheap here, with no one making a fuss about it.
The air smells of hot dust and machine oil. Nobody here is sentimental about the place, but they do not leave it either.

places.name: The Lift Head
places.text: A gantry of black girders where the ore cars unload onto the tugs. It is the loudest place on the planet and the best place to find a hauler who needs a hand.

places.name: Shaft Nine Canteen
places.text: A long low room cut into the rock, with a cooling duct that rattles overhead. The coffee is bad, the water is rationed, and there is always someone asleep at a table.

places.name: Spares Cage
places.text: A wire-fronted store of salvaged parts, run by crews who will happily take your old pump in exchange for a worse one.

people.name: Marit Vosk
people.text: She has worked the night-side seams since she was a girl and treats the dark as her own. She remembers every crew that left and every one that did not come back.
people.line: If you've brought water, sit down and I'll buy. If you haven't, sit down anyway, and you can explain yourself.
people.look: A woman in her fifties, broad and weathered, with a grey crop and soot worked into her knuckles. She wears a patched orange coverall with a heat-scorched collar and a lamp strapped to her forehead. A welded steel tag hangs from a bootlace around her neck.

people.name: Dennick Ashe
people.text: He flies ore from the lift head to the refinery and back. He knows the routes better than the charts do, and trusts neither.
people.line: Cinder's ore is the cheapest thing in the system. The food I bring down is the dearest, and nobody's complained yet.
people.look: A lean man in his thirties with a sunburned neck and sharp eyes, in a flight jacket with the sleeves cut off. A long burn scar runs up his left forearm. He keeps a cold pipe in his teeth.

people.name: Oyelaran Pike
people.text: He runs the only clinic on the night side, with a cabinet of medicine that is never quite full. He asks every pilot who comes in what they are carrying.
people.line: Medicine, if you've got it. Or water. Or a kind word, but I'd rather have the medicine.
people.look: A tall, stooped man in his sixties with dark skin, grey stubble and tired kind eyes. He wears a stained white apron over an orange coverall and has reading glasses pushed up into his hair.

rumors: They say the Blackhulls drop cargo at the far shafts when the Federation patrols come near, and nobody asks who collects it.
A survey crew went down a dead shaft last year and came up quiet. Now the shaft is welded shut and nobody will say why.
Prism sent a clean-suited man to look at the ore seams. He left in a hurry, and the crews are still arguing about why.
ports.vista: A night-side field of black rock under a thin amber haze. Welded orange-lit hab modules cling to the tunnel mouths in the foreground, scorched at one end and frosted at the other. Ore cars run on rails toward a tall girder lift that rises into a dark sky. A faint orange glow along the horizon marks the day side and the unseen star.

description: Halde Landing is the only real town in Brannock. Terraces of habitat blocks step down a cold coast, each one welded to the last and painted whatever colour was left over. The landing field is cut into the cliffs above them. Under low cloud and a pale orange sun, the sea below is a hard blue, and the beaches are grey and cold.

Most of the system's people live here, and most of its money changes hands in the market halls beside the field. Consumer goods are cheap in them and food is dear. The halls sell everything the mines and the yards cannot make: cloth, crockery, music, toys. The stall holders will tell you with a straight face that all of it was made locally.
Evenings on the terraces are loud. Shift crews come in from the other worlds, the bars fill, and the lamps come on in sodium orange, one block after another down the cliff.

places.name: The Market Halls
places.text: Long welded sheds beside the field, stacked with goods and crowded with bargaining. The roof leaks in three places and everyone knows which.

places.name: Cliff Stairs
places.text: A zigzag of steel steps between the landing field and the lowest terrace. Locals climb them without noticing. Visitors stop halfway.

places.name: The Cold Coast Bar
places.text: A long room bolted to the cliff edge, with a window that looks out over the grey sea. It is full from the end of the day shift until very late.

people.name: Ines Calloway
people.text: She buys and sells for half the stalls in the halls. She says she is retired, and nobody believes her.
people.line: Food's dear this season and goods are cheap. Funny how it's always the other way round for the people who buy.
people.look: A woman in her forties, short and round, with bright eyes, dark curls tied in a scarf, and rings on every finger. She wears a quilted orange jacket patched at the elbows. A pencil is always behind her ear.

people.name: Tobiah Rune
people.text: He checks cargo on the field for the town council. He is honest, which makes him rare, and tired, which makes him polite.
people.line: I don't care what you carry, as long as it's what the manifest says it is. That's the whole job.
people.look: A man in his late fifties, thin and stooped, with a grey moustache and a weathered, careful face. He wears a council-issue coat in faded rust with a clipboard strapped to the forearm.

people.name: Wren Adeyemi
people.text: She left a rebel ship under circumstances she describes only as 'a disagreement about the food.' She now drinks quietly and listens a lot.
people.line: I've seen what the Federation does to a quiet system. Brannock's quiet. Enjoy it.
people.look: A woman in her late twenties, wiry, with close-cropped hair dyed a faded green and a sharp, watchful face. She wears a salvaged flight vest over a plain shirt. A torn strip of dark cloth is knotted around her wrist.

rumors: The Federation navy wants a permanent post on Halde. The council keeps losing the paperwork.
A trader swears he saw a Glass relay beacon blinking out past the gas giant. Nobody else has.
Someone in the market halls is selling goods with no stamp on them. The council pretends not to see it.
ports.vista: A landing field cut into pale cliffs, its pad lights glowing orange against a cloudy sky of blue-grey and low gold. Terraces of welded habitat blocks step down toward a cold dark-blue sea, their lamps just coming on. The market halls are long rusted sheds at the field's edge. A slow orange sun sits low behind the cloud.

description: Tallow is a small grey moon of Vast, and almost everything on it is a refinery. Tall towers burn off their waste in orange flares, and Vast hangs overhead, huge and banded, adding its own warm light. The domes are patched and re-patched, and the streets between them run with condensation. The light never quite gets to grey.

Ore from Cinder comes in raw and leaves as metal, and the air in the dome tastes of it. Metals and chemicals are cheap here, and everything the refiners need to keep working is dear: ore, water, food. The crews have a habit of tallying what each pilot brings in without saying it aloud.
It is a small colony, close-knit and short-tempered. The work is hot, loud and dull, and the people accept that. Visitors are fine so long as they do not stand in the way of a ladle.

places.name: The Casting Floor
places.text: A vast shed where molten metal is poured into moulds. It is hot and deafening, and the whole colony gathers to watch when the big pours begin.

places.name: Flare Street
places.text: The main way through the dome, lit all night by the orange of the burn-offs. Stalls selling hot food and bad coffee line both sides.

places.name: Vast Watch
places.text: A patched observation blister on the dome's top, where off-shift workers sit and look at the gas giant. Someone has painted a small arrow on the floor: 'You are here.'

people.name: Hollis Brandt
people.text: He has run the main stack for longer than most of the crew has been alive. He says he will retire when the refinery does.
people.line: Bring ore and water and I'll talk all day. Bring neither and I've got a stack to mind.
people.look: A heavy man in his sixties with a bald head, a grey beard stained at the edges, and deep lines around his eyes. He wears a heat-blackened apron over a patched orange coverall, and his left glove is welded at the cuff.

people.name: Sadie Quill
people.text: She tests every batch that leaves the moon and refuses to sign off on a bad one. Her stamp is respected from Cinder to Kettle.
people.line: Don't ask me whether it's good. Ask me whether it's good enough, and I'll tell you honestly.
people.look: A narrow woman in her thirties with sharp features, dark hair under a respirator hood, and ink-stained fingers. She wears a stained white lab coat over orange work trousers and keeps a row of vials clipped to her belt.

rumors: The Bloom has been seen, they say, far out past Vast. No one on Tallow will say it aloud, but the night crews keep a lamp lit.
Prism offered the refinery a new process and the foreman threw the offer into a smelter.
A Blackhull ship came in with a hold of nothing and left with a hold of metal. The tally sheet disagrees with itself.
ports.vista: A grey cratered moonscape under a huge banded sky of cream and brown, where Vast fills a third of the heavens. Refinery towers rise from the dome complex, their flares throwing orange light on rust-streaked plating and wet grey rock. The landing field is a flat of scorched concrete with welded pipe-racks and cable runs across it.

description: Kettle Yard is a cradle of girders, and the Ironhulls build and patch their hulls inside it. The station is welded together from whatever the last yards left behind: old gantries, scrapped ring sections, a crane arm from some forgotten dock. It has never been finished, and nobody expects it to be.

Metal comes in from Tallow, and ships go out. The yard pays well for metals, alloys and components, since a hull is only as good as its stock. It has little to say about water or medicine, which it does not trade. Everything else passes through, one way or another.
Arcs flash all through the cradle, and the sound of hammering carries even through the corridors. It is an honest place. A ship built here may be ugly, but it will hold.

places.name: The Cradle
places.text: The great open frame where hulls are built. Half-finished ships hang in it like ribs, with welders crawling over them on tethers.

places.name: Scrap Hall
places.text: A long gallery of salvaged plate, tubing and frame, sorted by weight and rust. The yard hands buy from it by eye.

places.name: The Tether
places.text: A bar on the cradle's rim, named for the safety line the welders clip on before they come in. Nobody has ever stopped doing it.

people.name: Gideon Marsh
people.text: He has laid seams on half the hulls that fly out of Brannock. He can tell a Kettle weld from across a dock.
people.line: Pretty doesn't hold, friend. Ugly holds. Look at the seam, not the paint.
people.look: A stocky man in his fifties with a shaved head, a broken nose, and forearms scarred by sparks. He wears a leather-patched orange apron and a flip-up welder's visor pushed back on his head.

people.name: Petra Lindqvist
people.text: She tracks every plate and bolt that enters the cradle. She is small and brisk, and she is never wrong about the stock.
people.line: You want a refit? Tell me what you've got first. Then we'll discuss what you want.
people.look: A slight woman in her forties with straight black hair in a tight knot, tired eyes, and quick hands. She wears a patched coverall in faded orange with a tablet strapped to her wrist and a pencil through her hair.

people.name: Joss Harker
people.text: He sits in the corner of The Tether and arranges things. He is polite, and nobody has ever seen him pay for a drink.
people.line: Plenty of work out there for a pilot who doesn't ask the wrong questions. I can point you at some.
people.look: A lean man in his thirties with a narrow smile, slicked dark hair, and a coat too clean for the station. A thin black band is stitched into his sleeve, and he turns a steel washer over and over in his fingers.

rumors: They say a new hull is under way in the deepest part of the cradle, and the yard hands who work on it do not talk at the bar.
The Federation wanted to inspect the yard's books. Petra Lindqvist gave them very thorough books indeed.
A Freeflag cutter limped in last month with its hull cut open, and left again before anyone had finished the welding.
ports.vista: A great open cradle of rusted girders, with half-built hulls hanging in the frame and welding arcs flashing blue-white across them. Sodium lamps wash the plating orange. Beyond the open dock, a dim orange star burns low and the scorched curve of Cinder hangs in the dark. Docking arms and patched gantries cross the foreground.
